hook.line: A visitor asks Tomás how the café works, and Mariana's article needs a tidy description. Spanish has set phrases for saying what something is made of and what it is called.
hook.es: El menú se divide en desayunos, almuerzos y postres.
hook.en: The menu is divided into breakfasts, lunches and desserts.

examples.es: El libro se divide en tres partes.
examples.en: The book is divided into three parts.

examples.es: El edificio se compone de cuatro pisos.
examples.en: The building is made up of four floors.

examples.es: El equipo está formado por seis personas.
examples.en: The team is made up of six people.

examples.es: El menú se divide en desayunos, almuerzos y postres.
examples.en: The menu is divided into breakfasts, lunches and desserts.

examples.es: Se le llama tinto al café negro que se toma en Colombia.
examples.en: The black coffee people drink in Colombia is called tinto.

examples.es: Esta parte de Bogotá se conoce como La Candelaria.
examples.en: This part of Bogotá is known as La Candelaria.

rule:
A handful of phrases for describing and classifying, all neutral-to-formal.

*Se divide en…*: the parts it is split into.
*Se compone de…* or *está formado por…*: what it is made of.
*Se conoce como…*: what it is known as.
*Se le llama… a…*: the name comes first, then *a* and the thing named: *Se le llama tinto al café negro.*

The small words are fixed: *dividir en*, *componerse de*, *formado por*. English "into" and "of" don't always match.
smallPrint: Teachers call *se divide* and *se compone* the pasiva refleja, the *se* passive for descriptions.

options: The book is divided into three parts.
The book is made up of three people.

readAndPick.es: El edificio se compone de cuatro pisos.
options: The building is divided into four owners.
The building is made up of four floors.

readAndPick.es: El equipo está formado por seis personas.
options: The team is made up of six people.
The team is known as six people.

options: This part of Bogotá is known as La Candelaria.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence: El libro ___ en tres partes. (se divide / se conoce)
yourTurn.answer: El libro se divide en tres partes.
yourTurn.why: For splitting into parts you need *se divide en*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The menu is divided into breakfasts, lunches and desserts.
yourTurn.answer: El menú se divide en desayunos, almuerzos y postres.
yourTurn.why: *Se divide en* followed by the parts.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The building is made up of four floors.
yourTurn.answer: El edificio se compone de cuatro pisos.
accept: El edificio está formado por cuatro pisos.
yourTurn.why: *Se compone de* says what it is made of.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The team is made up of six people.
yourTurn.answer: El equipo está formado por seis personas.
accept: El equipo se compone de seis personas.
yourTurn.why: *Formado por* is the other way to say what a group is made of.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: This part of Bogotá is known as La Candelaria.
yourTurn.answer: Esta parte de Bogotá se conoce como La Candelaria.
accept: A esta parte de Bogotá se le llama La Candelaria.
yourTurn.why: *Se conoce como* gives the usual name.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Black coffee is called tinto in Colombia.
yourTurn.answer: Se le llama tinto al café negro en Colombia.
accept: Al café negro se le llama tinto en Colombia.
En Colombia, al café negro se le llama tinto.
En Colombia se le llama tinto al café negro.
yourTurn.why: The name comes first, then *al* and the thing it names.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The class is divided into two groups.
yourTurn.answer: La clase se divide en dos grupos.
yourTurn.why: *Se divide en* works with any whole and its parts.

pitfalls.wrong: El libro se divide a tres partes.
pitfalls.right: El libro se divide en tres partes.

pitfalls.wrong: El edificio se compone en cuatro pisos.
pitfalls.right: El edificio se compone de cuatro pisos.

pitfalls.wrong: Se le llama el café negro tinto.
pitfalls.right: Se le llama tinto al café negro.
pitfalls.why: Spanish puts the name first, then *a* plus the thing named.

personal: Describe a place you know, such as your home or your town, with *se compone de…*, *se divide en…* or *se conoce como…*
